facts.statement: Zhongjianosaurus was first reported in 2009 from lake deposits in Sihedang, western Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Zhongjianosaurus was first reported in 2009 when a new species based on a specimen consisting of a partial postcranial articulated skeleton was recovered from the lake deposits in Sihedang, Lingyuan County, in western Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The genus was first described by Xu Xing and Qin Zi-Chuan.
facts.quote: It was first described by Xu Xing and Qin Zi-Chuan.

facts.statement: The name honors Yang Zhongjian, the founder of Chinese vertebrate paleontology.
facts.quote: The genus and specific name honor Yang Zhongjian, China's founder of vertebrate paleontology.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, IVPP V 22775, is housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, labelled as IVPP V 22775, is currently housed in the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, in Beijing.

facts.statement: Zhongjianosaurus is believed to come from the middle of the Jehol Biota in the Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: Believed to hail from the Yixian Formation, specifically the middle of the Jehol Biota

facts.statement: Zhongjianosaurus lived between 125 and 121 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian to Aptian) in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Zhongjianosaurus yangi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Zhongjianosaurus de dinosaurio terópodo dromeosáurido que vivió desde principios a mediados del período Cretácico entre 125 a 121 desde el Barremiense al Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Bone fusion in the holotype suggests it was a mature adult weighing 0.31 kg.
facts.quote: Bone fusion in the scapula, vertebrae, coracoid, and tarsals suggest that the specimen is a mature adult weighing 0.31 kg

facts.statement: The sternum has a maximum anteroposterior length of 56% of the femoral length.
facts.quote: The sternum is large, with a maximum anteroposterior length 56% of the femoral length

facts.statement: Zhongjianosaurus has proportionally long ossified uncinate processes fused to the dorsal ribs.
facts.quote: Proportionally long ossified uncinate processes are fused to the dorsal ribs.

facts.statement: The foot exhibits the arctometatarsalian condition.
facts.quote: The foot shows the arctometatarsalian condition.

facts.statement: Zhongjianosaurus is classified as a dromaeosaurid belonging to the Microraptoria.
facts.quote: Zhongjianosaurus is a genus of dromaeosaurid belonging to the Microraptoria.

facts.statement: Some studies suggest an alternate classification for Zhongjianosaurus as an avialan.
facts.quote: Some studies offer an alternate position as an avialan.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Zhongjianosaurus was possibly omnivorous and arboreal due to its small size.
facts.quote: Zhongjianosaurus was, in view of its small size, possibly omnivorous and arboreal.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding finger identification, with the authors proposing digits two, three, and four while most researchers identify them as one, two, and three.
facts.quote: The authors identify the fingers in the maniraptoran hand as the second, third and fourth, whereas most researchers see them as the first, second and third so that "metacarpal II" would become metacarpal I etc.

facts.statement: Zhongjianosaurus was first reported in 2009 based on a partial postcranial articulated skeleton recovered from lake deposits in Sihedang, Lingyuan, in western Liaoning province.
facts.quote: Zhongjianosaurus fue reportado por primera vez en 2009 cuando se recuperó una nueva especie basada en una muestra constituida por un esqueleto articular postcraneal parcial de los depósitos lacustres en Sihedang, Lingyuan, en el oeste de la provincia de Liaoning.

facts.statement: The species was described by Xu Xing and Qin Zi-Chuan.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por Xu Xing y Qin Zi-Chuan.

facts.statement: The genus and species name honor Yang Zhongjian, the founder of vertebrate paleontology in China.
facts.quote: El género y el nombre de la especie son en honor de Yang Zhongjian, el fundador de la paleontología de vertebrados en China.

facts.statement: The articulated tail features elongated rod-like extensions and chevrons characteristic of most dromaeosaurids, reaching almost to the anterior caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: La cola articulada tiene extensiones alargadas en forma de varilla y cheurones característicos de la mayoría de los dromeosáuridos, y éstas alcanzan casi los caudales más anteriores.

facts.statement: The sternum is represented by a large left sternal plate with a maximum anteroposterior length of 56% of the femoral length and is proportionally axially long.
facts.quote: El esternón está representado por lo que probablemente es la placa del esternón izquierdo. Es grande, con una longitud anteroposterior máxima del 56 por ciento de la longitud femoral y es axialmente larga en proporción.

facts.statement: Five left sternal ribs are preserved, which is more than observed in related genera Microraptor and Sinornithosaurus.
facts.quote: Se conservan cinco costillas esternales izquierdas, más de lo que se observa en los géneros relacionados Microraptor y Sinornithosaurus.

facts.statement: Studies by Xu and Qin place Zhongjianosaurus in the family Dromaeosauridae and specifically in the clade Microraptoria based on synapomorphies and cladistic analyses.
facts.quote: Estudios por Xu y Qin sitúan a Zhongjianosaurus en la familia Dromaeosauridae, y específicamente en el clado Microraptoria basándose en sus sinapomorfias y en los análisis cladísticos.

facts.statement: Some studies offer an alternative classification of Zhongjianosaurus as an avialan.
facts.quote: gunos estudios ofrecen una posición alternativa como avialano.

facts.statement: Zhongjianosaurus lived during the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The discovery of Zhongjianosaurus in the Yixian Formation alongside eight other dromaeosaurids suggests there was sufficient niche partitioning available.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Zhongjianosaurus en la Formación Yixian, además de otros ocho dromeosáuridos sugiere que había una cantidad suficiente de nicho de partición.

rejected.statement: Zhongjianosaurus is the smallest known microraptorine and one of the smallest non-avian theropod dinosaurs discovered.
rejected.quote: it is the smallest known microraptorine thus far discovered and one of the smallest non-avian theropod dinosaurs.
